With two laps to go, and Dave Holt leading into the first bend, the pace seemed to falter momentarily and in an instant brother Bob stepped smartly round the leader and hugging the kerb as he sped round the bend opened up 10 yards before John had stepped clear and gathered himself for pursuit.

A smaller than usual field of about 110 started off on the first of the three muddy laps, and at the end of the initial circuit we clearly had a fight on our hands, leading H/W by only 79-81. Gerry North and Tony Fairclough were setting the pace in company with Valentine and D.
Gerry North was also in fine form and was keeping the Bels well to the forefront, but the stage belonged to Dave Holt who ran into second position for Hercules/Wimbledon.

RIGHT: Bill Dance takes the lead for the first time and Pat O'Connor sets off leaving Dave Holt (HW) on the line. Moments later, Holt was in the lead which he stretched to give his club a winning margin.
Lionel Mann was an impressive winner of the first stage, but by the third leg Dave Holt had taken Hercules-Wimbledon into their winning lead: they are a difficult club to beat over six stages.

Dave Holt gained a little ground for Hercules who were still third. Stage 6 saw Hercules make a strong bid for the lead with a record breaking run by Mike Beevor who started 58 secs behind Bill Dance and brought his team up to a mere 9 secs behind us.

We had a quartet at Parliament Hill attempting a fifth successive win in the Greater London Council championship, while Hercs.Wim had their brilliant trio of Bob and Dave Holt and Mike Beever wearing E.C.C.U. colours on the Continent.
John was another having his first outing in this race, and what an initiation it was! As he waited to start he found himself alongside McAndrew (Reading), Ford (Aldershot), Watson (Cambridge) & D.
Gerry did not let his discomfort worry him and running his usual gritty race he maintained our position and held off Dave Holt, who had taken over a mere 8 seconds behind him.

So a great day for Belgrave and Oliver having the satisfaction of adding his name to a cup with such greats as Chris Chataway (1949), Tim Johnson (1959), Dave Holt (1964), Pete Standing (1968), Dave Clarke (1977) and Roger Hackney (1978).
